events.name: Ancient Lava Tube
events.intro: A cooled lava tube winds into the hillside like the throat of something asleep. Somewhere inside, rock ticks as it cools, a slow uneven clock. A geologist sits at the mouth with a clipboard on her knees and soot on her cheek. Geologist: "It's a shortcut. Mostly cooled." She taps the clipboard. "Mostly is doing a lot of work in that sentence, I'll admit."

choices.label: Walk the tube. (Fire damage to everyone but Fire-types)

success.text: You walk it. In places the floor is warm through your boots, and once it is hot, and your team skips across a seam of dull orange that should not still be glowing. Everyone comes out the far side singed and blinking at the daylight.
You take the long way over the top. It costs you the afternoon, and a lot of climbing, and the view at the top is so good that nobody minds as much as they expected.

choices.label: Lead with it; it feels the hot spots. (Fire or Rock)

branches.text: Your Pokémon goes first, one careful step at a time, pausing, turning, sniffing the stone. Wherever it steps, the floor is cool. The team walks in its footprints and comes out the far side without a mark. The geologist, behind you, is writing very fast. On the far side, your lead noses something out of the ground and brings it to you, very pleased with itself. Then someone you have never met stops you with a hand on your arm. "That's ten. Ten times I've heard of a trainer letting their Pokémon lead people through the worst of it." They pin a faded ribbon to your lead: the Pathfinder ribbon. Your lead stands a little straighter, and from now on it is quicker on its feet.

events.name: Fog Bank Navigation

events.name: Bakery Gift
events.intro: A bakery doorway, warm air spilling out of it into the cold, and the smell of it stops your whole team in its tracks. The baker, a round man in a floury apron, is handing buns out to anyone with a Poké Ball on their belt. Fen-Lo: "Trainers eat free on Thursdays." He winks. "It's always Thursday for trainers." Behind you in the queue, a small boy is counting coins in his palm, and coming up short.

success.text: You take one. It is still hot, sweet, soft in the middle. You break pieces off for your team as you walk, and everybody walks a little lighter.

You put the coins on the counter anyway. Fen-Lo looks at them for a long moment, and then at you, and something in his face goes soft. Fen-Lo: "Nobody ever pays." He puts two more buns in your bag when he thinks you are not looking.

events.name: Pokémon Center Lady
events.intro: A roadside first-aid post, really just a folding table, an awning and a kettle. A woman in a cardigan is knitting behind it, and a Chansey sits beside her with a tray of bandages on its lap. A hiker with a sprained ankle is waiting on the bench, pretending not to be. Mrs. Pryor: "Would you like me to heal your Pokémon? Sit, sit." She is already putting the knitting down.

success.text: She sees to every one of them, slowly, talking to each the whole time. Chansey hums. By the end your team is whole, and you are holding a cup of tea you do not remember being given.

Mrs. Pryor looks at you over her glasses, and then at the hiker, who goes red. She sees to his ankle first. Then your team. As you leave, the hiker limps after you to shake your hand, and says he'll not forget it. You think he means it.

She laughs, delighted. "Nobody's ever offered!" She heals your team, and you come back that evening, the long way round, with a sandwich wrapped in paper. She eats half and gives the other half to Chansey. It is the happiest you have seen anyone all week.

events.name: Gift from Mom
events.intro: A parcel waiting for you at the Pokémon Center counter, battered from the road, your name on it in handwriting you would know anywhere. Inside: two pairs of thick socks, a bottle of Sweet Berry Juice, a bag of the biscuits you liked when you were seven, and a note. "Don't forget to eat. I'm proud of you. Call." You read it twice. Your team crowds round the box, very interested in the biscuits.

success.text: You find the phone in the corner before you can talk yourself out of it. It rings twice.

You sit down at the Center's table and write back, a long letter, longer than you meant, about the road and the team and the things you have seen. You put it in the post with a drawing your lead "helped" with.

You tip the biscuits out on the floor of the Center and everybody gets one, then two, then the crumbs. It is a small thing. Your team acts like it is a feast. Afterwards they are all lying on your feet.

events.name: A Bigger Parcel

Inside are socks, more biscuits, two bottles of Sweet Berry Juice, a scarf that is clearly the first scarf anybody ever knitted, and a note: "Your letter is on the fridge. The drawing too. Tell your Pokémon it's very good. Keep writing."

success.text: You will. You put the scarf on, though it is not cold, and it is a bit lopsided, and you leave it on all day.

events.name: Kind Hiker
events.intro: A hiker on a bench at a bend in the trail, boots off, toes wriggling, a huge bag of trail mix open on his knee. He sees you and holds it out before you can say hello. Gus: "Trail mix? Got too much. Always do." He shakes the bag. "My wife says I pack for a family I haven't got."

success.text: You take a handful. Gus nods, satisfied, like a man who has done his job for the day.

choices.label: Swap him for something of mine.

success.text: You give him something from your bag in return. Gus turns it over in his big hands, and grins. Gus: "Fair trade. Fair trade!" He tells everybody he meets for the rest of the week.
You crouch and hold your palm out to your lead, who eats every last nut with enormous seriousness and then licks your hand. Gus laughs till he has to put his boots back on.

events.name: Pokémon Ranger
events.intro: A ranger at a lookout tower, binoculars round her neck, sleeves rolled up. Ranger Sol: "Mind if I check your team? Feet, eyes, teeth." She nods down the slope, where a wild Pokémon is lying in the grass, licking a cut on its leg. "Got one more patient waiting, but I've time."

success.text: She checks every one of them, quick and gentle, and finds things you never noticed: a stone in a paw, a scratch under a wing. When she is done, everybody is right as rain.

Sol looks at you properly, then nods once and goes down the slope. You watch her clean the cut and bind it while the wild Pokémon holds very still and trusts her. Then she comes back up and does your team. Ranger Sol: "Don't see many who'd wait."
She shrugs, cheerfully. "Suit yourself. Watch the left fork, it's muddy." She goes back to her binoculars.

It's not much.}" They push something into your hands. {rival}: "Good luck out there."

You dig in your bag and hand them something of yours. They blink at it. Then they put it away very carefully, in an inside pocket, and do not say anything, and that is how you know.
{rival}: "Wow." They shake their head. "Wow." They put the gift on the fence post anyway and walk off without looking back. You take it. It is a long time before you stop feeling bad about that.

events.name: The Last Cookie
events.intro: A rest stop, after a long day. One last cookie on the plate. It sits there. Every single member of your team is looking at it, and then at you, and then at it. Nobody moves. The silence has weight.

success.text: Your starter takes it with the dignity of the first. The others sulk, briefly, theatrically, and then one by one they curl up against your starter anyway, because that is where they always end up.
You break it into tiny, ridiculous, fair pieces and give everybody one. It is about one crumb each. It is the best crumb any of them has ever had.
You eat it. Every eye in the camp follows it all the way into your mouth. Nobody says anything. Nothing else happens. You feel terrible for the rest of the night.

events.name: Pay It Forward
events.intro: A shop counter. You put down a bag of Berries and reach for your money, and the shopkeeper shakes her head and slides a note across. "Paid for. Somebody before you." The note, in pencil: "Pass it on!"

choices.label: Pass it on. (pay for the next person, ₽150)

success.text: You take your bag, and then you put down money for whoever is next, and write "Pass it on!" on the back of the note. The shopkeeper pins it to the till. As you go, a tired-looking woman with a pram comes in, and you hear the shopkeeper start to tell her.
You take the Berries and keep the money. It was meant for you, after all. You think about it for a mile or two.
You run outside, but whoever it was is gone. Under the shop's mat there is a second note, as if they knew: "Don't find me. Pass it on."

events.name: Passing It On
events.intro: A stage on from the shop with the note, a noodle stall at dusk. A weary traveller in a coat too thin for the weather is counting coins on the counter, and counting them again, and coming up short. The stallholder is waiting, not unkindly. The traveller starts to push the bowl back.

success.text: You put the money down before they can finish pushing the bowl away. The traveller looks at it, and at you, and then they are crying, quietly, into the steam. They eat every noodle. When they leave, they shake your hand with both of theirs.
You put down half, and they manage the rest, and the two of you eat side by side at the counter without saying much. It is a good bowl.
You look away and walk on. Behind you, you hear the stallholder say something, and the traveller laugh, short and surprised. Maybe it worked out.

events.name: Mom Calls
events.intro: The phone rings. You know who it is before you pick up. Mom: "Are you eating well? Are you warm enough? Is your Pokémon eating well?" A pause. "I saw you on the news. Well, someone who looked like you. From the back. I told everyone at work it was you." She is quiet for a moment, and you can hear the kitchen behind her, the radio, the tap dripping that nobody ever fixed.

success.text: Mom: "You sound tired." You tell her you are not, and she does not believe you, and somehow, after you hang up, you are a bit less tired anyway.

choices.label: Tell her the truth about the road.

success.text: You tell her. The cold nights. The battles you lost. The one you almost did not get up from. She listens to all of it without saying a word. Then, Mom: "Come home whenever. Or don't. I'm proud either way." You put the phone down and sit for a minute with your team pressed against you.

You hold the phone out. Your starter makes its noise down it, loud and proud and very close to the receiver. On the other end there is a pause, and then your mother is laughing, and laughing, until she is crying, and you are too, a little.

events.name: Nurse Joy's Clinic
events.intro: A small clinic at the edge of town, a friendly doctor and a very long queue: a farmer with a limping Mareep, a girl with a sneezing Pichu, an old man who mostly seems to be there for the company. Dr. Amari sees you at the back and raises her voice. Dr. Amari: "I'll get to you. Or," she holds up a roll of bandage, "you could help me get to everyone faster."

success.text: You wait your turn on a hard bench and read a very old magazine. When your turn comes, she is quick and kind with your team, and they come out whole.

You roll your sleeves up. You hold Pokémon still, fetch things, comfort the girl with the Pichu. The queue goes down twice as fast. At the end of it, Dr. Amari heals your team herself and presses a Sitrus Berry into your hand. Dr. Amari: "Come back any time. I mean it. I'll put you on the rota."
You pay the fee to go first. Dr. Amari takes it without comment. Your team is healed. The queue watches you leave, and you can feel every one of them watching.

events.name: The Charity Drive
events.intro: A trestle table in the square with a hand-painted sign: FOR THE ORPHANAGE. A quiet woman in a grey coat sits behind it with a cash tin and an old leather ledger, writing names in very small, very neat handwriting. Hettie: "Whatever you can spare." She looks up. Her eyes are kind and tired. "Or not. That's alright too."

success.text: You put it in the tin. Hettie writes your name in the ledger, and the amount, and then, after a moment's thought, a little star beside it.
You put it in the tin, and Hettie stops writing and looks at the money, and then at you. Hettie: "That's… that's a winter's coal." She writes your name very carefully, and underlines it.
You give something from your bag. Hettie writes it down, exactly what it was, and thanks you for it as if it were gold.
Hettie: "That's alright too." She means it. She goes back to her ledger, and you go on.

events.name: One Umbrella, Two Trainers
events.intro: Rain, suddenly and all at once. You get your umbrella up. Under a tree by the road, a stranger in a long coat has no umbrella at all, and is standing very straight, getting very wet, with the patience of somebody who has been rained on many times before. Your whole team looks up at your umbrella, and then at the stranger, and then at you.

success.text: You walk over and hold it over them both. You walk to town together, close, shoulders bumping. They talk the whole way, in a slow voice, about old things: who built the bridge, what the river was called before it was called anything, the shape of something huge they once saw on the hills at dawn. At the town gate they thank you and go, and you realise you never asked their name.

You hand it over and walk on in the rain. Your team huddles under your coat. You get soaked. Later, on a bench at the edge of town, you find a smooth grey stone left where you will see it, still damp, still cool: a Damp Rock, and a dry bit of paper under it that says "thank you".
You keep walking. When you look back the stranger is still there, under the tree, very straight, in the rain.

events.name: The Charity Remembers
events.intro: Late in the region. Someone is waving at you from across the street, a quiet woman in a grey coat. Hettie, from the orphanage stall. She crosses through the traffic with the old leather ledger under her arm. Hettie: "Your kindness came back to us. Let us return the favour." She opens the ledger. Your name is in it, again and again, in her small careful handwriting: every kind thing you did on this road that anybody saw, and some that you thought nobody did.

branches.text: Hettie: "No. That's why." She presses a parcel into your hands: a Rare Candy, a Lucky Egg, and, folded very carefully, a drawing in crayon. It is you, and your team, very large, walking over a hill with the sun behind you. In the corner, in a child's writing: "THANK YOU". Hettie: "The children did it. They argued about the colours for a week."

effects.text: The orphanage children drew you and your team walking over a hill, the sun behind you

branches.text: Hettie: "No. That's why." She presses a parcel into your hands: a Rare Candy, and a Lucky Egg wrapped in a clean handkerchief.
Hettie: "No. That's why." She presses a Rare Candy into your hand and closes your fingers round it.

success.text: Hettie: "No. That's why." She presses something into your hands and will not take it back.

Hettie reads it. She reads every line, in order, in a soft voice, standing in the street with people going past. It is long. It is longer than you thought. By the end, your lead is leaning against your leg, and you are not quite looking at her.

You shake your head and push it back. "The orphanage. Please." Hettie looks at you for a long moment, and then she writes one more line in the ledger. A week later a letter finds you on the road. Inside, folded, is a crayon drawing of you and your team, and a child's writing: "THANK YOU".

events.name: The People You Helped
events.intro: The night before the worst of it. You are checking your team for the hundredth time when you hear voices at the edge of camp, and footsteps, a lot of footsteps. People are coming up the road with lamps.

branches.text: It is everyone. Fen-Lo the baker with a basket. Gus the hiker with too much trail mix. Ranger Sol, already rolling her sleeves up. Hettie with her ledger. Faces you helped without thinking about it, faces you had forgotten, all of them carrying lamps, a long line of light coming up the road behind you. Ranger Sol: "We heard where you were going. Thought you'd want company." Tomorrow, wherever you do not stand, one of them will. Nobody gets left behind this time.

effects.text: Everyone you were kind to came up the road with lamps the night before the crisis

branches.text: Fen-Lo the baker and Gus the hiker, arguing cheerfully about whose food is better, and behind them Ranger Sol with a medical bag. They feed your team, and Sol checks every paw and wing. Ranger Sol: "Tomorrow, if you have to split your team, I'll take the half you can't. Don't argue."

effects.label: Ranger Sol has your back: your team takes less damage

branches.text: Fen-Lo the baker, with a basket of buns still warm in a cloth, and Gus the hiker with a bag of trail mix the size of a pillow. Gus: "Packed for a family I haven't got. Turns out I have." Your team eats until it can't, and sleeps like it hasn't in weeks.

success.text: It is only one or two, in the end: a familiar face, a thermos of tea, a hand on your shoulder. It is enough.

remembers.notice: At the back of the line, in a coat too thin for the weather, is the traveller from the noodle stall. They do not say anything. They just stand with you, and hold a lamp.

events.name: Barefoot Monk
events.intro: A monk in faded saffron sits at the foot of a long hill, one foot bound in a strip of cloth, gone dark with blood. His staff is broken beside him. Far above, at the top of a thousand worn steps, a shrine roof shows between the pines. Brother Tal: "I must reach the shrine before the moon is full." He says it without self-pity, as a fact. "Can you carry me?"

success.text: You carry him. A thousand steps. He is lighter than he looks and heavier than you hoped, and he does not complain once, only hums an old tune under his breath that keeps time with your feet. At the top, he puts his hand flat on the shrine's gate, and turns to you, and tells you one true thing about where an old power sleeps in this land. You will remember it.

Your strongest Pokémon kneels without being asked, and Brother Tal climbs on, and they go up the steps together at a slow, careful walk. At the top he bows to your Pokémon before he bows to you, and tells you both one true thing about where an old power sleeps in this land.
Brother Tal: "Of course." He nods, and there is nothing in it but kindness. When you look back from the bend in the road, he has started up the steps on his own, one at a time.

events.name: Describe the View
events.intro: A viewpoint at the top of a pass, the whole valley laid out below in gold and green. An old woman sits on the bench with her hands folded on a white cane and her face turned to the wind. Marguerite: "I can't see it, but I can hear it." She tilts her head at the valley. "Rivers. Birds. Something big, far off. Tell me what's out there?"

success.text: You sit down and tell her. You do it badly at first, and then better, the river like a dropped ribbon, the town like spilled sugar, the shadow of a cloud walking over the fields. She listens with her whole face. Marguerite: "You've a good eye." In return she tells you a story her grandmother told her, about something small and bright that lives in this valley and is only seen by people who are not looking for it.

You describe your team instead, one by one. She asks each one's name, and says it back to them, slowly, getting it right. Each of them comes and puts its head under her hand when she says it. At the end she tells you a story about this valley that her grandmother told her, and you think the team listens as hard as you do.

You tell her there is a dragon on the far hill, sunning itself. She laughs, a big surprising laugh. Marguerite: "There's no dragon. But thank you." She pats your hand. Then she tells you about a wood where the trees repeat what trainers say, a season late. "Go and say something good there," she says.

events.name: Old Lady at the Crossing
events.intro: A busy road, cars and carts and a bus going by much too fast. An old lady stands at the kerb with a shopping basket and a stick, waiting for a gap that is never going to come. She takes a step, and steps back.

success.text: You offer your arm and she takes it, and you walk her across, slowly, one hand up to the traffic. On the far side she pats your arm twice. Old lady: "My late husband walked like you. Like the road was yours." She tells you, as you go, that her husband used to say three old spirits keep the lakes of this land, and that you had best be good to lakes.

choices.label: Stop the traffic with a big Pokémon.

success.text: You send out your biggest Pokémon and it walks into the middle of the road and sits down. Everything stops dead. The drivers glare. The old lady laughs so hard she has to lean on you, all the way across. On the far side she tells you her husband used to say three old spirits keep the lakes of this land, and that you had best be good to lakes.
You point her to the crossing, fifty yards down. She thanks you and goes. She gets there.

events.name: Old Man's Tale
events.intro: A campfire at a rest stop, and an old man already sitting at it, poking it with a stick. He has kept a place for you, or for anyone. Hob: "You've got time for a story." He does not look up. "Everyone has, if they stop."

success.text: You sit, and he tells it: an old story about the great one of this region, how it came, what it wanted, where it went to sleep. He tells it like a man telling you about his own grandfather. It is a long story. You will find out, later, that every word of it is true.

You tell him one of yours, about the road and your team, and he listens to all of it, nodding. Then he tells his: an old story about the great one of this region. Hob: "I'll tell yours to the next one who stops. That's how it works." Somewhere, later, a stranger is going to hear about you.
Hob: "Fair enough." He keeps the fire going for you while you sleep, and in the morning he is gone, and the fire is still warm.

events.name: Quiet Hermit
events.intro: A hollow tree with a door in it, a real door, painted green, with a brass knocker. A thin man with a beard down to his belt opens it before you knock and looks at your bag. Wennick: "Bring food, and I'll tell you my story." He clears his throat. "I don't get many visitors. I'm out of practice at asking."

success.text: You give him three Berries. He eats one very slowly, with his eyes closed, and then he tells you his story: thirty years ago, on this very hill, at dawn, he saw something he could not name, and it looked at him, and he has been waiting here ever since in case it comes back.

You cook. He eats as if he has forgotten how food tastes. Afterwards, by the fire in his tree, he tells you his story: thirty years ago, on this hill, at dawn, something he could not name looked at him, and he has waited for it ever since. Before you go he gives you a Leftovers. Wennick: "I won't need it. Someone's coming. I can feel it."
Wennick: "Come back when you've some." He closes the green door very gently.

events.name: A Meal on the Road
events.intro: A traveller at the side of the road, cooking over a fire so small it fits in two hands. A dented pot, something simmering. They look up as you pass and shift along the log. Traveller: "There's always enough for one more. Sit."

success.text: You sit. The pot should not feed two, let alone your whole team, and somehow it does. While you eat, the traveller talks about a Pokémon they saw once, white and gold, walking on the water of a lake at dawn, not hurrying. Traveller: "It looked at me like I was enough." They do not explain, and you do not ask.

choices.label: Add something to the pot. (an Oran Berry)

success.text: You drop a Berry in. The traveller smiles like you have given them a gift. The meal is enough for everyone, and then some, and your team is so full and so warm that they all fall asleep in a heap against the log. The traveller tells you about something white and gold they saw once, walking on water at dawn.
Traveller: "Another time." They mean it. When you look back, they are still there, the little fire still going.

events.name: Camp
events.intro: A tidy camp set up for travellers: a ring of stones round a firepit, a tent pitched square, a kettle on a hook. A camp warden in a wide hat checks you in with a clipboard. Camp warden: "One hour, then I need the pitch." She looks at your team, already spreading out to sniff everything, and softens. "Or the whole night, if you need it. What'll it be?"

success.text: You make camp. Nobody says much. Your team lies down round you by the fire, one by one, and sleeps the deep sleep of the safe, and so does anyone travelling in your care. In the morning everyone is whole again.
You spread your gear out on the grass.
You sit down in the middle of your team and wait for them to tell you.

choices.label: Talk by the fire. (evening or night)

success.text: The fire burns low. You take one of them a little way off, where it is quiet.

events.name: Camp Council
events.intro: A quiet camp between two roads, an hour to spend, and your whole team looking at you to decide how to spend it. They each make their case. Your starter paces, restless, wanting to train. The newest one keeps bringing you sticks to throw. The one who has been with you longest is already lying down with its eyes half shut, making a very clear point.

success.text: You train. An hour of hard work, sharp and focused, and your lead comes out of it standing differently, ready for anything. The newest one sulks under a bush with its stick.

effects.label: Trained hard: your lead hits harder

success.text: You throw the stick. And again. And again. By the end of the hour the whole team is playing, even the old one, and the newest is so happy it can barely stand up. Afterwards nobody wants to stop.
You sleep. All of you, in a heap, in the sun. The old one gets the best spot, against your side, and sighs a long sigh of having been right.

events.name: Words with the Mentor
events.intro: Your mentor talks best at night, when the road is quiet and the fire is low and there is nobody else to hear. They sit with their hands round a tin cup and do not look at you. Mentor: "Ask me anything. Once." A long pause. "I'll answer straight."

success.text: Your mentor thinks for a long time. Then they tell you, plainly, about what is waiting at the end of this road: what it fights with, what it holds back, where it is weak. It is a true answer. You can tell by how much they did not want to give it.

A long silence. Then your mentor tells you. Not all of it. One thing, from a long time ago, that they have not told anyone. When they are done, they finish their cup and go to bed without another word, and the next morning they are a little easier with you.
Mentor: "Yes." They look at you, finally. "Don't let it slow you."
Your mentor looks at you for a long moment over the cup, then nods. Mentor: "You're ready."

events.name: Around the Fire
events.intro: An hour off, and your Pokémon drift toward each other the way they do. Two are squabbling over the warm rock. Three are playing some game with rules only they understand. And one is off by itself at the edge of the firelight, watching the others, not joining in.

success.text: You sit down between the two and do not take sides, and after a while they are sharing the rock, and after a while longer they are asleep on it, curled round each other. Whatever was between them is gone.
You join the game. You do not understand the rules. You lose, badly, every round, and every single one of them thinks it is the funniest thing that has ever happened.
You go and sit with the one at the edge. You do not say anything. After a while it leans against you, just a little, and you stay like that until the fire goes down.

events.name: Before You Go
events.intro: A quiet road ahead, an hour to spare, and your gear spread out on a groundsheet. What you can usefully do with an hour changes as the day wears on.

success.text: You leave the team at camp and walk the road ahead, and come back with the next stretch drawn on the back of your hand.
You tip the bag out and sort it, properly, for the first time in weeks. At the bottom, squashed but whole, is something you forgot you had.
You mend what can be mended by the light of the fire, and your team rests and gathers itself. Everyone will go into the next fight fresh.
Today is a day worth marking, and you mark it. The whole team feasts by the fire, and in the morning a stranger has left a small gift by the ashes.

events.name: About the Rival
events.intro: The fire pops. Your starter, lying with its chin on its paws, gives you a look that you have learned means one thing. It is thinking about {rival}. So, if you are honest, are you.

success.text: You say it out loud, for the first time. They are good. Better than you, some days. Your starter thumps its tail once, agreeing, and it is easier to say than you thought.
They are annoying. You list the ways. It takes a while. Your starter listens to the whole list with great patience, and then yawns.
You do. You do not know when that started. You sit with it, and your starter comes and leans on you, and neither of you says anything else.

events.name: A Rival's Trail
events.intro: A quiet clearing. One of your team stops in the middle of the path and will not move. It has been like this since the last time it faced that one Pokémon of your rival's, the one it always ends up facing. It scratches a shape in the dirt with one claw: the other Pokémon's shape. Then it looks up at you.

success.text: You train for it. Every move that one makes, you make, and your Pokémon answers it, over and over, until the answers come without thinking. When you leave the clearing it is walking taller, and its eyes are fixed on the road ahead.

effects.label: Trained for its rival: hits harder next fight

success.text: You sit down by the shape in the dirt and talk to it, about losing and about trying again, and about how you do not care who wins, not really. It listens. Then it rubs the shape out with its tail.

You sit on a log and let it think. It is remembering the one that took the blow meant for it, and did not get up. It takes a long time. Then, all at once, it gets up and comes to you, ready, and the whole team gathers round it.

choices.label: Ask about the one that left.

success.text: Its rival joined a trainer, and it has not known what to do with that. You tell it that it is allowed to miss an enemy. It sits with you for a while, and something in it settles.

events.name: Quiet Talk
events.intro: Away from the others, the night is long enough for a real conversation. You sit with one of them on a rock at the edge of camp, the fire behind you and the stars in front, and it is the kind of quiet where you can say things.

choices.label: Ask about where they came from.

success.text: You ask, and it shows you, the only way it can: the way it looks at the dark, the direction it faces, the sound it makes very softly in its throat. You remember the day you found it, and you understand that it remembers too, from the other side. You have never felt so much that it chose you.

You tell it about home. Your room. The window. The tree in the yard. The sound the kettle makes. It does not understand a word, and listens to every one, its head on your knee. One by one the others come over from the fire and listen too.
The fire pops. You find you are thinking about {rival}.
Your mentor has been watching the fire too.

events.name: Mom Calls
events.intro: The phone rings. You know who it is before you pick up. Mom: "Are you eating well? Are you warm enough? Is your Pokémon eating well?" A pause. "I saw you on the news. Well, someone who looked like you. From the back. I told everyone at work it was you." She is quiet for a moment, and you can hear the kitchen behind her, the radio, the tap dripping that nobody ever fixed.

success.text: Mom: "You sound tired." You tell her you are not, and she does not believe you, and somehow, after you hang up, you are a bit less tired anyway.

choices.label: Tell her the truth about the road.

success.text: You tell her. The cold nights. The battles you lost. The one you almost did not get up from. She listens to all of it without saying a word. Then, Mom: "Come home whenever. Or don't. I'm proud either way." You put the phone down and sit for a minute with your team pressed against you.

You hold the phone out. Your starter makes its noise down it, loud and proud and very close to the receiver. On the other end there is a pause, and then your mother is laughing, and laughing, until she is crying, and you are too, a little.
